name: FlySBS Aviation Limited
summary:
Research hold, not a buy or an allegation. FlySBS grew FY26 revenue 64.3% to ₹318.5323 crore and reported PAT ₹60.7734 crore, but its dry-lease transition absorbs aircraft deposits and entry-into-service (EIS) cash that a simple CFO-minus-PPE screen misses. Reported ₹65.2412 crore cash is not equivalent to available bank cash. [S1]

BQS4.8/10, GQS5.0/10 after persistent-cash-conversion cap; IAS NS. G1/G2/G4 Conditional; G3 Hold—unresolved. No evidenced G1 or G3 failure is asserted. The decisive missing evidence is timely access to short/pledged/long deposits and the actual bank/obligation position after documented sanction dates, not an assumed absence of accounting equity.

A month-end-funded conditional base, with explicit FD access and no new borrowing, produces 14.58% annualized return at 12×terminal LTM EBIT over 19Oct 2026–31Oct 2031, below the 15% hurdle. Without a ₹5 crore early non-earmarked FD bridge it has a ₹3.1484 crore cash gap; strict no-setoff access produces ₹39.5849 crore. A restrained no-discretionary-growth survival case is funded under the same favorable access assumptions, so unresolved access is not automatic insolvency. The ordinary linked bear is unfunded and receives no ordinary target/IRR. [E_MODEL, E_STRESS]

What could improve the conclusion: bank confirmations and FD release mapping, funded aircraft cohorts, sustained cash realization after deposits/EIS, independently reconciled bank-stock statements and subsidiary/GST scope. What invalidates it: denied essential cash access, material unexplained loss of deposits or falsified financing/counterparty evidence.

sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Identity: FlySBS Aviation Limited, NSE EMERGE FLYSBS, ISIN INE0VCK01011, incorporated 7Aug 2020, listed 8Aug 2025. Chartered non-scheduled aviation is the economic archetype; lease rent remains an operating cost. Audited accounts use Accounting Standards under the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, not an assumed Ind AS 116 right-of-use/debt model. Legal identity is verified; no similarly named company substituted. [S1, S2]

Information cutoff 20Oct 2026; last official close 19Oct 2026₹597.40, not last traded ₹600. October 20 is an exchange holiday. Quote is historical EOD, not live/executable. Sources were retrieved 21Oct but only documents available by cutoff inform facts. September 29 presentation future October 15 milestone is not retrospectively treated as accomplished. Latest financial baseline is audited 31Mar 2026; H1FY27 results not available in reviewed cutoff records. H1FY26 is historical limited-review information, not a current TTM update. [M1, M6, S6, S10]

Scope: standalone operational accounts. Board/secretarial disclosures say Dubai wholly owned FlySBS Aviation LLC was incorporated 3Feb 2026 with AED100,000 capital and no business; CARO states no subsidiaries and balance sheet investment is nil. We do not add nonexistent subsidiary profits or pretend this is a clean consolidated history. Its funding and presentation need reconciliation. Model reserves ₹0.25 crore incremental subscription, a bounded estimate, not a verified INR conversion. [S1 pp 56,76,86; S5]

Confidence: historical transcriptions High where clear, cross-period comparability and operating economics Medium; overall financial interpretation Medium; current funding/valuation Low. All 13 factors are shown; R is NS. Four gates and resolution evidence are in the structured register. BQS/GQS quality-only comparison is eligible at Medium confidence because all quality factors are scoreable and G2 is Conditional, not a central reliability failure. IAS investment ranking remains excluded while G3 is unresolved. Funding uncertainty is not an automatic exclusion from historical quality comparison.

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factors (score/confidence): GOV5/M, MOAT4/M, REV8/M, DUR6/M, CAP5/M, CASH2/M, BAL3/M, EXEC5/M, EARN5/M, R NS/Low, D2/M, P4/M, L7/M. Each is linked to evidence and an independent rationale in factor_audit. No historical 9–10 assigned without a full comparable cycle.

BQS: GOV1.00+MOAT0.80+REV0.96+DUR0.60+CAP0.60+CASH0.20+BAL0.24+EXEC0.40=4.80, final/display 4.8;100% factor coverage.
GQS: REV3.20+DUR1.20+EARN0.75+CAP0.75+CASH0.20=6.10 raw. Persistent CASH2 imposes the explicit growth-quality cap 5.00, display 5.0. Not a generic SME discount.
IAS known contributions: unrounded BQS4.80×25%=1.20; D2×20%=0.40; P4×10%=0.40; L7×10%=0.70. Known 2.70, coverage 65%, missing R weight 35%; mathematical missing-data bound[3.05,6.20]. IAS stays NS, not the midpoint, not the lower bound and not an automatic 3 funding cap. No G1/G3 Fail means no governance/funding numerical cap is applied.

Judgment sensitivity: GOV and CAP each ±1 move BQS by ±0.20 and ±0.12, joint range 4.48–5.12. GQS raw changes ±0.15 from CAP but remains capped 5.0. L ±1 changes known IAS contribution ±0.10 without making it scoreable. If access were independently supported and other assumptions unchanged, conditional 14.58% minus 15% hurdle is −0.42pp, corresponding to R5, not a current assigned score. No averaging BQS/GQS or extra narrative penalty.

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text:
FlySBS sells on-demand private/business aviation: corporate customers, high-net-worth individuals and other charter users purchase flights. Wet charter procures aircraft plus crew from third-party operators; dry lease requires FlySBS to arrange operations, crew, maintenance and aircraft availability itself. Dry leasing may improve control and unit margin but brings deposits, EIS expenditure, utilization and end-of-lease risks. Revenue is gross charter billing, not a platform fee or asset-light net take rate. Aircraft are not owned merely because called the company's fleet. [S1, S2]

The audited PPE ₹7.0973 crore comprises aircraft components/vehicles/other assets, not purchased jets. Aircraft security deposits ₹174.417 crore and EIS ₹24.4713 crore are central operating investment. Rentals, insurance, crew, fuel, maintenance, handling and airport charges recur; refundable deposits are neither perpetual free cash nor automatically available collateral. [S1 pp 104–115]

FY26 international revenue ₹276.179 crore,86.7%, domestic ₹42.3533 crore versus ₹44.6658 crore FY25. Corporate ₹293.612 crore,92.2%; repeat customer revenue ₹279.798 crore,87.8%. Repeat is a management-defined relationship indicator, not subscription ARR or guaranteed retention. Geography is exposure, not proof of a foreign moat. [S1]

At March 26, reports describe two dry leased aircraft and a wet-charter pool; March induction and June 1 commercial launch of Legacy 650 are distinct milestones. Targeted nine aircraft by March 27, seven dry/two wet, is management ambition. Readiness, permit, crew and revenue-start evidence for each future aircraft is required. [S1, S6, S13]

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The plausible advantages are aviation permissions, safety/crew systems, an operating record and access to long-range aircraft. These create execution hurdles but not demonstrated durable pricing power. Customers can use other charter operators, brokers or fractional programs; third-party aircraft supply remains concentrated. The dossier finds no independently proven market-share leadership, proprietary technology, exclusive network or consistently superior mature-cohort returns. MOAT4 reflects that distinction. [S1, S2]

Customer concentration was severe FY25: top 1 40.55%, top 5 90.54%, top 10 95.05%; top 1 FY24 45.15%, FY23 46.16%. Supplier top 1 38.39%, top 5 86.39%, top 10 93.56%. IPO risk disclosures describe absence of binding long-term customer and supplier contracts. FY26 repeat business does not establish that concentration fell; current customer identities, connected-party checks and cohort retention remain ND. [S2]

The prospectus says no listed company has a directly comparable business. Global Vectra is an adjacent listed aviation reference, but helicopter offshore oil-and-gas/onshore services differ in aircraft, contracts and utilization economics. Scheduled passenger carriers and cargo airlines likewise are not automatic charter valuation peers. Management's anonymized comparison and private fractional-ownership competitors do not supply a defensible P/E median. Accordingly no peer financial-multiple bonus is awarded;12×EV/EBIT is an analyst scenario tested at 8–14×, not a market-derived fact. [S2, P1]

Disconfirming moat evidence: recurring high customer concentration, limited contractual duration, foreign operating exposure and dependence on lessor/maintenance access. A sustained full-cost per-aircraft return spread and repeated wins at stable realized yields would be stronger evidence than fleet count or reported ROCE.

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Historical standalone revenue, crore: short FY21 15.94879; FY22 27.23729; FY23 34.1072; FY24 106.4869; FY25 193.8956; FY26 318.5323. Annual additions FY22–26:11.28850,6.86991,72.37970,87.40870,124.63670. Three-year FY23–26 CAGR is 110.6%; four full-year FY22–26 CAGR84.9%. Arithmetic five-year CAGR82.0% uses a short first fiscal period and is explicitly not an annual like-for-like growth claim. No ten-year history exists. [S1, S2, S8; verified_inputs]

Pre-IPO restated revenue accelerated before the August 25 IPO; FY26 is the first listed fiscal year, not evidence of a manufactured post-listing step by itself. Chargeable hours rose from 522h 18m FY23 to 1486h 08m FY24 and 2600h FY25. Implied revenue/hour approximately ₹6.53/7.17/7.46 lakh reflects geography, aircraft and charter mix, not pure pricing. FY26 management says hours more than doubled without an exact consistent numerical bridge; exact volume/price/acquisition contribution is ND. [S2, S1]

H1FY26 revenue ₹137.6064 crore versus ₹83.7122 crore; PAT ₹23.8434 crore versus ₹5.2035 crore. FY26 less H1 implies H2 revenue ₹180.9259 crore/PAT ₹36.9300 crore. This subtraction is not an independently audited H2 statement and is not annualized into FY27. [S10, S1]

Source inconsistency matters: annual strategy narrative gives dry-revenue share 25.09%; AGM revenue-stream figures ₹110.7 crore/₹318.5 crore imply 34.75%, versus ₹77.4 crore/₹193.9 crore≈39.9% FY25. Do not explain all margin improvement as a proven rising dry share. Revenue growth is demonstrated, but precise unit mix and sustainability require reconciliation. REV8 respects the exceptional growth while capping confidence for scale/model change.

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Accessible growth comes from funded aircraft availability, chargeable hours, customer demand and pricing after full lease economics, not a generic aviation TAM. The nine-aircraft March 27 timetable is not orders or contracted revenue. A delayed aircraft may preserve cash temporarily while postponing earnings; maintenance downtime, permissions and crew limitations can produce the opposite cost/earnings pattern. We do not convert fleet targets directly into sales. [S1, S4, S6]

Capital efficiency includes cash tied in aircraft/custom/rental deposits, EIS and working capital. FY26 aircraft deposits ₹174.417 crore, supplier advances ₹34.3323 crore, inventory ₹18.5045 crore and EIS ₹24.4713 crore refute a simple asset-light interpretation. Adjusted operating invested-capital proxy rises from ₹129.6783 crore FY25 to ₹291.3137 crore FY26. It excludes reported cash, tax-authority assets, accrued FD interest and deferred IPO cost, and deducts operating trade/other liabilities excluding interest. It retains aircraft deposits and operating EIS. [S1]

Normalized operating EBIT FY25₹39.2697 crore to FY26₹70.0741 crore; at 25.17% tax, incremental NOPAT/ΔIC≈14.26%. FY26 NOPAT/average IC≈24.91% is a separate average-return proxy, not proof new jets earn 25%. The 12–16% nominal INR WACC range is an analyst hurdle cross-check, not an observed company cost. Latest incremental spread straddles that range. Three-/five-year incremental-return claims are NM without a comparable mature fleet and operating-capital bridge across the wet/dry transition. CAP5, not a high-ROCE shortcut.

The forecast explicitly funds ONWC at 25.44% sales, PPE0.7% sales, new EIS1% sales, and growth deposits 20% incremental sales from FY29. First two years assume existing deposits/IPO deployment cover capacity, a material unverified sufficiency assumption; requiring fresh deposits from year 1 creates a ₹4.5191 crore shortfall even in base. Thus growth runway and financing cannot be scored independently.

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Balanced governance finding: audited opinion is unmodified; CARO reports appropriate inventory verification with no material discrepancy, no reported fraud/default and no identified audit-trail tampering. The auditor's May 26 one-year-liability assessment is favorable, but is not an October bank confirmation. These facts prevent equating issues with fraud. [S1 pp 80–87]

Bank stock submissions were below, not above, books: Q1 books ₹8.9093283 crore/submitted ₹8.8684192 crore; Q2₹14.5025/₹8.9259563, gap ₹5.5765437; Q3₹14.5044836/₹14.5044836; Q4₹18.5044836/₹14.5407448, gap ₹3.9637388 or 21.42% books. Issuer says it submitted the extent adequate for drawing power, not an itemized reconciliation. Request period-by-period stock categories and lender acceptance; do not call this inflated collateral or a physical-stock fraud. [S1 pp 82–83]

Related-party capital advance to Shreshtha ₹5 crore versus ₹3.2852 crore, and Chryseum advances ₹7.0099 crore advanced/returned, vehicle ₹1.4243 crore and consultancy ₹3.0417 crore require commercial terms and delivery evidence. Director remuneration ₹0.5377 crore is not itself disproportionate to reported earnings. Promoters hold 32.47%,5,618,998 shares; public 67.53%. Total locked-in 12,728,421 shares≈73.56%, including 7,109,423 public shares, so public percentage is not tradable float. No promoter pledge/NDU/other encumbrance reported March 26; later unlock/current ownership not assumed. [S1, S9]

Auditor succession: KRMM resigned 30Sep 24 citing personal/preoccupation; KEK resigned 4Feb 25 after partner departure/reallocation; AJM appointed February 25. These are disclosed explanations, not proof of a scope dispute. IPO litigation includes 12 cases against promoter-group member P Karthik Iyer Parasuraman, not cases against the issuer/directors/promoters in that table; do not transfer allegations/guilt to FlySBS. Current court status is unverified. [S2]

The January 26 proceeds-certificate clarification says CARE monitoring made a separate auditor certificate inapplicable; NSE receipt acknowledgement is not substantive adjudication. September AGM borrowing authority ₹500 crore is permission, not a loan sanction or liquidity. Dubai subsidiary and GST scope discrepancies remain specifically logged. [S5, S7, S11]

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Earnings bridge, FY26 crore: reported PBT80.9151; subtract all other income 15.5891, including FX11.717 and interest 3.821; add back only IPO P&L amortization 1.9118. At normalized 25.17% tax this yields recurring PAT proxy ₹50.3140 crore, not reported ₹60.7734 crore. Normalized operating EBIT70.0741 adds borrowing interest 2.8363 but keeps bank fees 0.4501 operating. Core EBITDA excluding other income 69.1831 is distinct from reported 84.7722. EIS amortization remains a cost. [S1]

IPO cost 14.0902=1.9118 expensed+12.1784 deferred (9.9155 noncurrent+2.2629 current), not a securities-premium deduction. Historical issue expenditure incurred is not added as future cash; its exact historical payment timing is not independently reconciled; deferred expenditure is excluded from capital support. EIS balance 24.4713 (21.328 noncurrent+3.1433 current) is amortized over 8 years and includes pre-operation rent/charter/crew. It can mask cash intensity even if accounting is disclosed. [S1 pp 94–95,108–121]

FX P&L gain 11.717 differs from cash-flow reversal 11.5179; ₹0.1991 difference is preserved. Foreign revenue and costs provide partial natural hedging, not zero exposure. FX outgo ₹196.8944 crore, foreign lease rental exposure and foreign aircraft deposits remain in analysis after excluding the gain from recurring earnings. A transient 10% unrepriced foreign-cost cash shock ₹19.6894 crore creates a ₹7.9931 crore funding gap; it is not a permanent net-INR currency forecast, has no assumed tax shield and does not rewrite terminal EBIT. Persistent rental-cost sensitivities separately reduce both cash and terminal EBIT. [S1]

FY26 CFO31.5422/PAT60.7734=51.9%; FY24–26 combined 33.14%. CF starts PBT80.9151, adds DA0.5707/gratuity 0.0275/finance 3.2864, subtracts unrealized FX11.5179/interest 3.821, giving 69.4608 before WC. Receivables consume 17.333, inventory 7.9968, supplier/other short advances 12.325; tax paid 9.9934. CFO −PPE capex=29.2995, but additionally deduct long advances 125.9664, other noncurrent cash 9.7135 and cash interest 3.2864: owner-cash broad proxy −109.6668. This includes growth investment, not a claim maintenance cash flow is equally negative. [S1]

Comparative controls: FY25 CFO0.5463 in FY26 AR versus 0.0114 IPO, difference 0.5349 prior-period adjustment; investing classification changes offset. FY25 capital advance 3.2851 moves from short to long advances, not new cash. FY26 inventory balance change 9.5952 differs from cash-flow 7.9968; long advances balance increase 135.9109 differs from cash flow 125.9664. FX/noncash effects may contribute, but no invented exact reconciliation is supplied. FY21–22 CFO classified long advances inside operations; do not splice into a six-year conversion ratio.

Receivables 38.2069:38.1975 less than 6 months after due date,.0094 six–12 months, none older/no provision. Average receivable days≈33.9FY26 versus 25.9FY25. Favorable ageing is not proof of final collection or connected-counterparty absence. Trade payables mainly under 1 year; ₹0.0087 crore 1–2 years. Year-end transaction-level sales and subsequent collections remain unavailable.

Claims/cash: reported 65.2412 comprises current-account/cash 0.1405, unpledged short FD4.25, pledged FD36.4365 and>12 month FD24.4142. Even 4.3905 short bucket requires FD redemption. Debt 36.6562 includes demand 34.2102 and term 2.446. ICICI validity 27Aug 26 and Kotak 15Oct 26 passed; no renewal assumed, no default inferred. GST CARO disputes 0.4746133 and Note 28 provision 2.1145645 have unitemized overlap with GST payable 2.931; TDS contingency 0.48 is separate. Opening payroll/statutory/tax/CSR/interest/gratuity/debt claims each receive one explicit cash or terminal treatment. Full no-overlap April GST stress is shown, not blindly double deducted. [S1]

sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹597.40 and 17,303,751 current issued shares, market capitalization is ₹1,033.7261 crore. Reported FY26 weighted EPS ₹38.76 uses 15,680,710 shares; current-share reported EPS is approximately ₹35.12 and recurring-proxy EPS ₹29.08. The IPO's 4,567,000 new shares increased the count by 35.86% over 12,736,751 pre-IPO shares. No outstanding options, warrants or convertibles were reported at March 2026; future financing can still dilute shareholders. [S1,S2,S9,M1]

Cross-checks: current-share reported P/E 17.01×; normalized P/E 20.55×; reported P/B 3.30×. Excluding deferred IPO expenditure, EIS and the related-party capital advance gives a book-support proxy of ₹272.0329 crore, or 3.80× P/B. This is not liquidation value: aircraft deposits and advances depend on contractual recovery. EV deducting all nominal cash is ₹1,005.1411 crore, not a liquidity-safe measure. Deducting only ₹4.3905 crore of short unpledged cash/deposits gives EV ₹1,065.9918 crore, 15.21× normalized EBIT and 15.41× core EBITDA. Even this deposit bucket is not verified immediately available. Neither convention invents an October net-debt figure. Rentals remain expensed and no lease debt is subtracted again. [S1,M1]

The model starts with the audited 31 March 2026 balance sheet and runs 67 months through October 2031. The price horizon is 19 October 2026 to 31 October 2031, approximately 5.032 years. All cases combine a hypothetical pre-entry stub with a forward path; they do not share one verified October balance sheet. The month-seven row is 31 October month-end, not a precise 19 October snapshot. No dividends are paid. Returns are nominal INR, before personal taxes and execution costs. Terminal multiples apply to the final twelve months' EBIT.

Base assumptions: FY27–32 revenue growth 20%, 20%, 18%, 15%, 12%, 10%; EBIT margin 20%; cash tax 25.17%; operating NWC 25.44% of sales; PPE cash investment 0.7%; new EIS cash 1%; growth deposits 20% of incremental sales from FY29. Existing deposits and remaining IPO deployment are assumed to fund earlier capacity. This is not independently established aircraft-level sufficiency. Revenue changes to the new fiscal-year run rate in April while incremental WC is phased monthly, another timing convention.

Funding assumptions are explicit and essential. Short FD ₹4.25 crore is available initially. All pledged FD ₹36.4365 crore releases or sets off demand debt ₹34.2102 crore in August 2026, including hypothetical early settlement of Kotak rather than waiting until its October validity date. A further ₹5 crore of non-earmarked long FD is redeemed in September, with the balance released in March 2028. No new bank borrowing is assumed. March unspent IPO cash ₹12.3549 crore is tracked within existing FD, not fresh financing: June deployment ₹0.63 crore occurs once, then the remaining ₹11.7249 crore is deployed on release with the earlier spending reimbursed once. Earmarked proceeds do not fund unrelated legacy tax. Term loans follow disclosed balances, rates and monthly payments.

Opening income tax ₹20.4449 crore and CSR ₹0.3301 crore are paid in September, other legacy statutory/payroll amounts in April, contingent TDS ₹0.48 crore in March 2027. Long-term gratuity and deferred-tax reserve ₹1.7046 crore are deducted at exit. Deferred tax is conservatively reserved without pretending an exact reversal schedule is known. The ₹1.8015 crore revenue-authority asset is neither offset against payment nor added to terminal value. Corporate-card payable ₹1.4766 crore is assumed normal non-interest-bearing operating float; interest-bearing revolving treatment would require a different financing bridge.

Base conditional terminal LTM EBIT is ₹147.5592 crore. At 12×, EV is ₹1,770.7105 crore; adding cash ₹281.0311 crore and subtracting senior reserve ₹1.7046 crore gives equity ₹2,050.0370 crore, or ₹1,184.74 per share and 14.58% annualized return. Minimum modeled month-end cash is only ₹0.9669 crore. Bull growth is 30%, 30%, 25%, 20%, 18%, 15%, with 22–23% margins and 14× LTM exit: ₹2,129.57 per share and 28.74%, still conditional on access. Ordinary bear receives no valid price or return because funding fails. No probabilities are assigned.

Reverse expectations: a 15% hurdle requires 12.2611× terminal LTM EBIT under the base cash path. Assumption-dependent entry prices for 12%, 15%, 18% hurdles are ₹669.80, ₹586.38, ₹515.11. The current ₹597.40 exceeds the 15% case. At 10× and 8×, base returns fall to 11.09% and 7.10%. The forward annualized-earnings alternative gives 15.34%, showing denominator sensitivity, not a second base. Constant-growth 10%, 15%, 20%, 25% versus 8×, 10×, 12×, 14× is fully tabulated. A 1% round-trip wealth haircut lowers base IRR to about 14.35%; actual spreads and impact are unknown. Missing funding evidence still makes R NS.

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
Permanent-loss risk: High. Linked bear assumptions are a 20% first-year revenue decline, flat second year, then 5%, 8%, 8%, 8% recovery; EBIT margins 10%, 10%, 12%, 13%, 13%, 13%; operating NWC seven percentage points above base; ₹2 crore additional annual operating cost; and 7× LTM exit. A customer loss or geopolitical disruption reduces utilization while fixed operating costs and slower collections consume cash together. First-month shortfall is ₹1.0641 crore, peak cumulative shortfall ₹10.3346 crore. Continuing to terminal value with negative cash is not funding. Ordinary bear price and IRR remain NS.

A separate hypothetical recapitalization supplies ₹10.3346 crore at ₹298.70 per share, half the entry quote, adding approximately 0.03460 crore shares. It produces terminal ₹206.60 per share and −19.02% annualized return, approximately 65.4% price loss. Injections occur in April and September 2026, before entry. This is a counterfactual opening-balance rescue illustration, not a completed historical issue or an assured future transaction. Its chosen subscription price can exceed bear recovery value and mechanically improve per-share recovery despite dilution; it is not a lower bound on future financing cost.

Restrained survival assumes revenue down 10% then flat, 15% margins, zero discretionary growth deposits, PPE spending 0.3% and EIS cash 0.5% of sales, while retaining all legacy and IPO commitments. At 8× exit it remains month-end funded under the same access assumptions, minimum cash approximately ₹1.165 crore, but yields ₹303.40 per share and −12.60% annualized return. Survival and attractive shareholder returns are different: this case loses approximately 49.2% of quoted price. It prevents an automatic G3 Fail conclusion.

Access stresses: remove the September ₹5 crore FD bridge and the base gap is ₹3.1484 crore; prohibit pledged-FD setoff and it is ₹39.5849 crore; delay access to the short unpledged FD and the gap is ₹3.2831 crore. Paying opening income tax in April instead of September produces a ₹19.8081 crore gap. Paying the entire separately named GST amounts in April without overlap produces a ₹1.6222 crore gap. Requiring a ₹5 crore minimum cash balance fails by ₹4.0331 crore. These are scenario-specific shortfalls, not evidence that historical default occurred.

The long-FD-never-released case still assumes recovery at par at exit, so it tests delay only. A separate zero-terminal-recovery case exists. Foreign-cost stress is a transient first-year cash shock without tax shield; rental cost tests reduce recurring cash and terminal EBIT. Neither proves an upper bound on unknown maintenance reserves, restoration payments or minimum contractual lease obligations.

Recovery support is uncertain: book equity includes aircraft deposits ₹174.417 crore, related-party capital advance ₹5 crore, EIS and deferred IPO assets. There is no independently verified liquidation valuation. Deposits are not added again to going-concern EV because they support modeled earnings. Temporary price volatility becomes structural impairment if deposits are lost, earning power is persistently damaged, or refinancing requires adverse recapitalization. Month-end funding does not prove intramonth payment capacity.

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
No supported five-year 5× or 10× claim. Required five-year price CAGR is 37.97% for 5× and 58.49% for 10×. Revenue growth, enterprise value, equity value and per-share returns must remain separate.

With no dilution, a 20× terminal P/E and 16% net margin, 5× price needs approximately ₹258.43 crore PAT and ₹1,615.20 crore revenue; 10× needs ₹516.86 crore PAT and ₹3,230.39 crore revenue. Relative to FY26 sales ₹318.5323 crore, required five-year revenue CAGR is 38.36% and 58.94%. These are algebraic requirements, not forecasts of demand or market share. A lower 15× exit P/E requires one-third more earnings and revenue. A 20% increase in shares requires 20% more earnings for the same per-share outcome.

The return identity is revenue growth × normalized net-margin change × initial/final diluted shares × exit/entry P/E. It must use recurring-proxy earnings, not reported FX gains or pre-IPO weighted-share EPS. The capital, aircraft availability, diversified customers and full-cost returns needed for these outcomes are not yet demonstrated. Even the favorable conditional bull reaches only about 3.56× price. Classification: Speculative / unsupported, with no defensible precise success probability. [S1,S2; model]

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
Monitoring recommendations, not scheduled automation:
1. Bank access and current cash. March baseline: demand debt ₹34.2102 crore and pledged FD ₹36.4365 crore; documented ICICI/Kotak validity ended August 27/October 15. Obtain dated confirmations, renewal or repayment records, FD release rights and a restricted/unrestricted map now. Missing evidence is an alert; demonstrated inability to meet essential obligations without rescue is a thesis break.
2. IPO objects. June unspent funds ₹11.72 crore; FD receipts ₹12.31 crore include interest and cash-credit money. CARE could not exactly trace the ₹0.63 crore bank-line-funded use. The next monitor should show bank-level allocation and a revised approved implementation timetable. Delay alone is an alert; unexplained diversion or material unreconciled cash is a gate issue.
3. Fleet commissioning. Verify induction, airworthiness, permissions and first paid flight separately for each aircraft. The March 2027 nine-aircraft goal requires actual commissioning and utilization evidence. A future milestone labeled as added is not proof of completion.
4. Core economics. Base normalized EBIT margin is 20%, not the FX-rich reported figure. Persistent margins below 15%, or unabsorbed maintenance/rental cost while capacity expands, challenge base economics. An isolated mix change calls for a unit bridge rather than automatic rejection.
5. Cash conversion. FY24–26 CFO/PAT is 33.1%; FY26 broad owner-cash proxy is −₹109.7 crore including growth investment. Seek improving collections and positive cash after essential EIS/deposit spending. Renewed growth without a funding bridge is a warning.
6. Customer concentration and collections. FY25 top customer was 40.55%; FY26 receivables were predominantly less than six months overdue. Obtain current customer/supplier concentration, connected-counterparty checks and subsequent receipts. A major customer loss with retained fixed costs activates the linked bear.
7. Bank-stock reconciliation. Q4 reported stock was ₹3.9637 crore below books. Obtain itemized stock categories and lender acceptance. Recurring unexplained gaps constrain GOV/G2 but do not automatically prove fraud.
8. Claims and scope. Reconcile GST disputes ₹0.4746 crore and provision ₹2.1146 crore with GST payable ₹2.931 crore; contingent TDS ₹0.48 crore; and Dubai capital/ownership/consolidation. Unfunded additional claims or different ownership of deposits would change gates.
9. Dilution and implementation. Before any trade, refresh issued shares, financing, lock-in expiry, promoter encumbrance, lot size, 20/60-session data and executable spread/depth for the actual position. The ₹5 lakh reference is not a suitability recommendation.
10. Related-party advance. Obtain milestones, commercial terms and settlement evidence for the ₹5 crore Shreshtha advance and consultancy arrangements. Unexplained extensions or write-offs change CAP/GOV; verified commercial delivery would reduce concern.

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Final classification: Research hold — unresolved funding access; mixed business quality with high cash-conversion and impairment risk. BQS 4.8 and GQS 5.0 are eligible for quality-only comparison: their factors have Medium confidence, and G2 is Conditional. This is not an investment endorsement. IAS is NS, and there is no favorable investment classification until critical funding evidence supports a return factor. The complete-score classification matrix cannot be forced onto an incomplete record.

For new research, prioritize bank, deposit and claims reconciliation before treating the quote as investable. A lower price does not resolve access. The conditional 15% hurdle entry of ₹586.38 is not an instruction to buy at that level. Even a verified funded base retains customer concentration, lease and execution risks. No allocation or personal suitability conclusion is made without the user's horizon, position size, risk tolerance and existing holdings.

If independent records establish cash access and funded aircraft cohorts, rerun from actual October balances rather than preserving the modeled stub. If ordinary operations remain unfinanceable after verified access and claims, G3 can become Fail; apply the IAS cap of 3 only if IAS is otherwise scoreable. Substantiated severe integrity evidence would activate G1/GOV overrides. Today's hold is not a disguised assertion of default or fraud.

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Source hierarchy: official NSE market data and signed annual accounts/prospectus first; CARE monitoring with its stated limitations; management presentations only as attributed claims; adjacent-peer business descriptions for qualitative context. Material factors link to structured evidence and source IDs. Retrieval on 21 October 2026 is distinct from the 20 October information cutoff. No later results, renewals or commissioning outcomes are backfilled.

The deliverable includes verified inputs, complete monthly cash/debt/share calculations, annual scenario bridges, sensitivities, opening claims and official market-session data. Every recorded creditor category receives one operating, payment or terminal treatment. Deposits remain operating capital rather than an additional target-value asset. Historical IPO expenditure does not become new forecast financing. The original assembled book is unchanged.

Critical open questions: actual bank balances and renewals; pledged-FD setoff and redemption terms; whether the ₹4.25 crore short FD is immediately available; mapping March IPO funds within long FDs; dated statutory and income-tax settlements; GST overlap; lease minimums, maintenance and restoration obligations; aircraft-deposit currencies and recoverability; funded capacity for the growth path; Dubai funding/consolidation; FY26 wet/dry revenue reconciliation; current concentration and subsequent receivable collections. No expired bank line is assumed to replenish cash after the hypothetical August repayment.

Additional limitations: monthly rather than intraday funding; no independent bank/auditor confirmation; short operating history and no full lease cycle; no clean directly comparable listed peer set; unknown spreads, impact and current lock-in/ownership changes. EIS amortization is scaled with sales rather than a detailed eight-year asset-cohort schedule; cash additions are separately deducted and no negative pool arises in the base horizon, but timing remains an assumption. Terminal cash is treated as surplus with no independently established operating-cash floor, and exit NWC follows the disclosed ramp convention. These matter for valuation confidence.

Missing evidence is ND or NS, never zero or a neutral score. An eventual favorable outcome would not retroactively fund an unsupported path. All modeled returns are before personal taxes, non-guaranteed and assumption-dependent. The model audit establishes arithmetic consistency, not the accuracy of unverified current funding assumptions.

gates.reason: No substantiated diversion, manipulation or minority abuse in reviewed records. Unmodified audit, no fraud reported, no promoter pledge; concentrated counterparties, RPT advance and disclosure discrepancies require continued verification, not an accusation.

Audited earnings can be normalized and cash buckets bounded. Below-book bank submissions, dormant subsidiary scope and GST-demand overlap are unresolved but not sufficient here to declare all accounts unusable. Escalate to Hold if account/reconciliation evidence contradicts ownership, receivability or material cash access.

Current bank access is critical and unverified after ICICI August27/Kotak October15 sanction validity. Conditional setoff plus5crore non-earmarked FD bridge funds base and restrained survival; base without early bridge has3.1484crore gap, strict-access39.5849, bear10.3346. These are conditional model deficits, not observed defaults, so not automatic Fail. Require bank confirmations, unencumbered deposits and dated obligations.

Official trades and60-session capacity exist, no ASM/GSM/ESM in relevant flags; official SME irregular-trading and high-low>75% cautions,20% band,200-share lot and unknown executable spread/depth prevent a Clear implementation conclusion.
